capabilities: Display notes in Parents, Children, Friends, and Siblings quadrants around the active note
Resolve relationships automatically from body links and configurable frontmatter properties
Compute sibling groups from shared parent notes
Suppress notes via Obsidian excluded-files settings or custom tag and filename blacklist rules
Collapse dense quadrant groups and inspect filtered nodes in a hidden-notes panel
extras: The README notes the repository triggers Obsidian's 'Vault Enumeration' submission notice because it reads all vault files, and points to a separate 'Technical Description' document for engineering details.
intentEvidence: Zsolt hinted at gatherings that it was time for a native implementation to take over, I accepted the challenge
motivation: The author, a healthcare professional who relied on structured parent/child/friend/sibling thinking, built a native implementation after ExcaliBrain's Excalidraw-based canvas proved limiting.
problem: Obsidian's core graph view shows links as a chaotic force-directed web, making hierarchical relationships hard to read in large vaults.

relations.evidence: If your existing structure is Excalibrain-friendly and front-matter based there would be little or no rewrites
the creators of TheBrain for proving that structured association is a beautiful way to organize

summary: Structured semantic graph view that arranges notes around the active note in Parents, Children, Friends, and Siblings quadrants.
